section: Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India 2001
title: Though the children’s population (up to 14 years age) as per census 2001 was 30.4 per cent of the total population, children accounted for 9.4 per cent in the proportion of victims of accidental deaths. In general males, accounting for 72.4 per cent of total victims were at a greater risk from accidents than females. Most of the victims of accidents were aged between 15 to 44 years. This group of people constituted nearly two-third (60.4%) of all persons killed in the accidents in the country. Causes of Accidental Deaths The percentage of ‘Accidental Deaths’ due to Natural Causes and those due to Un-Natural Causes were 13.5% and 86.5% respectively. The total deaths due to Accidents increased by 5.9 per cent over the previous year. However, the magnitude of ‘Accidental Deaths’ by Natural Causes increased by (111.1%) and that of deaths by Un-Natural Causes decreased by 1.7 per cent during 2001. The share of deaths due to Natural causes in total accidental deaths increased to 13.5 per cent compared to 6.8 per cent in the previous year. The share of deaths due to natural calamities such as ‘Earthquake’, ‘Avalanche’, ‘Lightning’ and Un- Natural causes such as ‘Collapse of Structure’, ‘Killing by Animals’, ‘Sudden Deaths’, ‘Mines or Quarry disaster’, ‘Falls’, ‘Poisoning’, ‘Factory/Machine Accidents’, ‘Killing by Fire Arms’ and ‘Rail-Road Accidents’ has increased. The same has decreased due to Natural causes such as ‘Flood’, ‘Starvation/Thirst’, ‘Torrential Rain’, ‘Cold & Exposure’, ‘Cyclone/Tornado’ and Un-Natural causes such as ‘Air Crash’, ‘Stampede’, ‘Explosion’, ‘Fire’, ‘Suffocation’, and ‘Drowning’, etc. The average rate of Accidental Deaths has marginally increased from 25.5 in 2000 to 26.4 in 2001 due to increase of rate for all major causes of Accidental Deaths. notes: Note : — (dash) stands for very negligible figure (less than 0.1)
Deaths due to natural causes has increased significantly by 111.1 per cent during 2001 as compared to year 2000. A major
Earthquake in Gujarat on 26th January 2001 was the contributory factor to this steep increase wherein 13,697 deaths (out
of 13,702 total deaths in the country) were reported from Gujarat.
Among the victims of natural calamities, nearly 63.0 per cent were males. Age-wise, nearly 15.0 per cent were children,
